use._comment: `plain_chapati_twice_a_week` was here, and it made this counter INFEASIBLE on every start date tried. The library rule means 'plain chapati on exactly two days; OTHER DAYS VARY', which presumes a bread slot that varies — and `constant_items` below pins `bread` to plain chapati on EVERY day. Five forced days against a cap of two: no menu can satisfy both. The pin is the client-specific, deliberate statement and the library ref is the copy-paste, so the ref went. The fleet shows the shape a daily bread pin takes — Booking.com and DXC both pin plain chapati daily and pair it with a staple/repeatable declaration, never with a frequency cap. No staple ref is added, because none is needed: a pinned cell is narrowed to its one dish and `unique_items` never sees it, which a solve with only this rule removed confirms. If the client ever does want a varying bread slot, the ref comes back and the pin goes at the same time — one without the other is this bug again.

rules._comment: Every Friday is a chicken gravy or dry. Which second day carries the other non-veg service is not yet specified, so no day restriction is applied.
rules.name: plum_nonveg_by_weekday

rules._comment: Client confirmed: ONE non-veg a week. The requirement names Friday ('every Friday chicken gravy/dry'), so the other four days are blank and plum_nonveg_by_weekday decides what Friday serves.
rules.name: plum_nonveg_fri_only
